original_value: Keeping the conversation consistent and avoiding its repetition are two key factors to construct an intelligent multi-turn knowledge-grounded dialogue system. Although some works tend to combine history with external knowledge such as personal background information to boost dialogue quality, they are prone to ignore the fact that incorporating the same knowledge multiple times into the conversation leads to repetition. The main reason is the lack of effective control over the use of knowledge on the conversation level. So we design a history-adaption knowledge incorporation mechanism to build an effective multi-turn dialogue model. Our proposed model addresses repetition by recurrently updating the knowledge from the conversation level and progressively incorporating it into the history step-by-step. And the knowledge-grounded history representation also enhances the conversation consistency. Experimental results show that our proposed model significantly outperforms several retrieval-based models on some benchmark datasets. The human evaluation demonstrates that our model can maintain conversation consistent and reduce conversation repetition.

result.paraphrase: To build an intelligent multi-turn knowledge-grounded dialogue system, it is crucial to keep the conversation coherent and avoid repeated content. While some methods merge dialogue history with external knowledge such as personal background information to improve response quality, they often overlook that reusing the same knowledge multiple times in a conversation causes repetition. This stems mainly from the absence of effective conversation-level control over knowledge usage. To address this, we propose a history-adaption knowledge incorporation mechanism for an effective multi-turn dialogue model. It reduces repetition by repeatedly updating knowledge at the conversation level and integrating it into the history incrementally, step by step. The resulting knowledge-grounded history representation also improves conversational consistency. Experimental results indicate that our model significantly outperforms several retrieval-based models on benchmark datasets, and human evaluation shows it can maintain consistency while reducing repetition.
